source_text: Sacerdos qui offert illud comedet. Qui verbum ministrat, vivat de evangelio. Non mercenarius sed pastor.
thought_title: The priest who offers eats; the minister lives by the gospel
orientation: Origen is applying the Levitical rule about who may eat the sacrifice to Christian ministers, contrasting the true pastor with the hireling.
pass_a_gloss: [The] priest who offers it [will] eat [it]. [He] who [the] word ministers, [let him] live from [the] gospel. Not [a] hired hand but [a] shepherd.

choices.english: The priest who offers it shall eat it
choices.why: Keeps the future force of comedet as a legal prescription, matching the Levitical rule being quoted.
rejected: The priest offering it will eat it
The priest who offers it eats it

choices.why: Ministers preserves the liturgical and service sense of ministrat, linking the Levitical priest to the Christian preacher.
rejected: The one who administers the word

choices.english: let him live from the gospel
choices.why: The subjunctive is hortatory or permissive, echoing Paul's rule about those who preach the gospel living by it.
rejected: he should live by the gospel

choices.english: Not a hireling but a shepherd
choices.why: Hireling captures the negative connotation of mercenarius as one who works only for pay, contrasted with the true shepherd.
rejected: Not a wage-earner but a pastor
Not an employee but a shepherd

bible_refs.note: Qui verbum ministrat, vivat de evangelio

pass_b_english: The priest who offers it shall eat it (Leviticus 6:26). He who ministers the word, let him live from the gospel (1 Corinthians 9:14). Not a hireling but a shepherd (John 10:12).
